newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks tumble as President Lee speaks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks tumble as President Lee speaks.

text.p: An early slide in Taiwan share prices deepened at midsession as President Lee Teng-hui took questions on live television at an annual news conference.
With 85 minutes left, at 0235 GMT, the index had tumbled 172.94 points or 2.11 percent to 8,008.68.
Turnover was a heavy T$70 billion.

"Investors are taking profits against Wednesday's gains because of a lack of confidence," said United Securities chief analyst Lin Long-hsien. "People are watching President Lee's news conference, but have not yet drawn any conclusions."
Lin said he did not rule out a slight rebound in the final hour of trading, citing expectations that government-related funds might intervene to boost the index for political reasons.

The electronics sector fell most sharply, losing 4.9 percent by midsession, while financial shares were up a modest 0.65 percent -- a rise that brokers cited as strong evidence that government intervention was under way.
Such intervention generally focusses on financial sector shares due to their heavy weighting in the index.

President Lee opened the news conference by affirming that embattled Premier Lien Chan, the focus of intense opposition and public criticism over a perceived breakdown in law and order, could resign upon completion of constitutional reforms in July.

Lee also offered his personal apology for what he called "problems of social order", a comment that market watchers, speaking ahead of the news conference, had said could help to strengthen investor confidence in the jitter stock market.
